# Installation

`rfaR` is currently not available on the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN). The package source code is available from the [USACE-RMC GitHub repository](https://github.com/USACE-RMC/rfaR).

## System Requirements

- R version 4.1 or later
- Internet access to reach the `USACE-RMC/rfaR` GitHub repository
- Recommended: IDE geared towards science & engineering, such as RStudio [RStudio](https://posit.co/products/open-source/rstudio) or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/)

## Install rfaR

### Install with remotes (recommended)

Install the `remotes` package and then install `rfaR` from GitHub:

```r
install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github(
  "USACE-RMC/rfaR",
  build_vignettes = FALSE
)
```

### Install with devtools (developers and contributors)

Users who plan to modify the package source should clone the repository and work from a local copy of the project. After cloning the repository with Git or GitHub Desktop, open an R session or RStudio Project from the repository root directory.

Install devtools if it is not already available (requires Rtools):

```r
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("USACE-RMC/rfaR")
```

During active development, load the package source into the current R session without installing it:

```r
devtools::load_all()
```

To install the local working copy of `rfaR` into your R library, run:

```r
devtools::install()
```

::: {.callout-note}
Cloning the repository does not make `library(rfaR)` available. To use the package, install it with `devtools::install()` or `remotes::install_github()`, or load the source for development with `devtools::load_all()`.
:::

## Dependencies

Required package dependencies are declared in the `rfaR` `DESCRIPTION` file and are installed automatically during installation. Installing `rfaR` with `remotes` or `devtools` installs required R package dependencies as needed.

USACE users may encounter package download, installation, or compatibility issues because of network controls, repository-access restrictions, or locally managed R environments.

To report an installation or version-compatibility issue, open an issue in the [rfaR GitHub repository](https://github.com/USACE-RMC/rfaR/issues). Include the R version, operating system, installation method, and complete error message when possible. Do not include Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), credentials, access tokens, or other nonpublic system information in a GitHub issue.

## Verify Installation

Load `rfaR` and confirm that the installed version and included example data are available:

```r
# Load package
library(rfaR)
# Check package version
packageVersion("rfaR")
# Print some example data
head(jmd_wy1980_stage)
```

If these commands run without error, rfaR is installed and ready to use.
